title: 卷耳
author: 佚名（《诗经·周南》）
authorEn: Anonymous (Book of Songs, Airs of Zhounan)
intro: A woman picking greens can’t fill her basket because she keeps thinking of her husband far away — then the poem jumps to him, climbing mountains on a worn-out horse, drinking to forget. One of the first poems to show two people missing each other at once.
analysis: 第一章写一个女子在路边采卷耳（一种野菜），采了又采，连一个浅浅的斜口筐都装不满，因为她心不在焉：她在想念远方的丈夫，干脆把筐放在大路边，望着远方发呆。后面三章画面一下子转到远方：一个男子正在翻山越岭，山越来越高，马越来越累，生了病，仆人也累倒了；他只好倒一杯酒，希望能暂时不那么想家。一个家里，一个路上，两个人同时在思念对方。这种“从对面写起”的写法——不写自己多想他，而写想象中他多想我——后来被很多诗人学习，比如杜甫的《月夜》。关于后三章是谁在说话，一说是女子想象丈夫的处境，一说是男子自己的口吻，两种读法都很动人。
analysisEn: In verse 1 a woman is picking juǎn’ěr, a wild green, by the roadside. She picks and picks but can’t even fill a shallow basket, because her mind is elsewhere — on her husband far away. In the end she just sets the basket down by the big road and stares into the distance. Then, in verses 2 to 4, the scene jumps to a man on a journey: the hills get steeper, his horse gets weaker and falls sick, his servant collapses, and he pours himself wine so he won’t ache with longing quite so much. One person at home, one on the road, each missing the other at the same moment. Writing about your longing by imagining the other person longing for you became a favourite technique of later poets — Du Fu’s “Moonlit Night” is a famous example. Who speaks the last three verses is debated: some say it is the wife picturing her husband’s hardships, others that the husband speaks for himself. Either way, the switch between the two scenes is what makes this old song so moving.
background: The Book of Songs gathers 305 songs from about the 11th to the 6th century BC. This is from the Airs of Zhounan (周南), songs from the lands south of the Zhou capital — the same section that opens with “The Ospreys Call”. The author is unknown.
pronunciation: 卷 juǎn；顷筐 qīng kuāng（“顷”通“倾”，斜口的筐）；寘 zhì；周行 zhōu háng（大路，“行”读 háng）；陟 zhì；崔嵬 cuī wéi；虺隤 huī tuí；罍 léi；兕觥 sì gōng；砠 jū；瘏 tú；痡 pū；吁 xū（忧愁）。生僻字机器朗读易错，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行《毛诗》文本，全诗四章，每章四句（第二、三章后两句为六言、五言）；网站按句读两句为一行排版。

lines.py: cǎi cǎi juǎn ěr, bù yíng qīng kuāng
lines.lit: I pick and pick the mouse-ear, yet do not fill my shallow basket.
lines.en: I pick and pick the mouse-ear greens, but my little basket won’t fill.

lines.py: jiē wǒ huái rén, zhì bǐ zhōu háng
lines.lit: Ah, I miss my man — I set it down by the great road.
lines.en: Oh, I’m thinking of him — I set the basket down beside the highway.

lines.py: zhì bǐ cuī wéi, wǒ mǎ huī tuí
lines.lit: I climb that rocky height; my horse is worn out.
lines.en: I climb the rocky heights; my horse is worn and weak.

lines.zh: 我姑酌彼金罍，维以不永怀。
lines.rhythm: 我姑/酌彼/金罍，维以/不永怀
lines.py: wǒ gū zhuó bǐ jīn léi, wéi yǐ bù yǒng huái
lines.lit: For now I pour from that bronze jar, so as not to long forever.
lines.en: For now I pour wine from the bronze jar, so the longing won’t last all night.
lines.tts: 我姑酌彼金雷，维以不永怀。

lines.py: zhì bǐ gāo gāng, wǒ mǎ xuán huáng
lines.lit: I climb that high ridge; my horse is sick and faded.
lines.en: I climb the high ridge; my horse is sick, its coat gone dull.

lines.zh: 我姑酌彼兕觥，维以不永伤。
lines.rhythm: 我姑/酌彼/兕觥，维以/不永伤
lines.py: wǒ gū zhuó bǐ sì gōng, wéi yǐ bù yǒng shāng
lines.lit: For now I pour from that horn cup, so as not to grieve forever.
lines.en: For now I pour wine from the horn cup, so the sorrow won’t go on and on.
lines.tts: 我姑酌彼四觥，维以不永伤。

lines.py: zhì bǐ jū yǐ, wǒ mǎ tú yǐ
lines.lit: I climb that stony hill; my horse is exhausted;
lines.en: I climb the stony hill — my horse is spent,

lines.py: wǒ pú pū yǐ, yún hé xū yǐ
lines.lit: my servant is sick — how sad I am!
lines.en: my servant is sick — how heavy my heart!

words.note: 动词重叠，表示一再采摘。
一种野菜，嫩叶可以吃，今天叫“苍耳”。

words.en: a shallow basket with a slanting rim

words.note: 兕：古书里的犀牛一类动物。

words.en: (of a horse) sick, its colour gone dull
words.note: 古义；后来“玄黄”多指天地。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 山越爬越高，路越走越难，表示远行人的辛苦和离家越来越远。
imagery.en: Ever higher hills and harder roads: the traveller’s hardship, and the growing distance from home.

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: 马累病了，仆人也累倒了，人的疲惫和思念都借马写出来。
imagery.en: The horse falls sick and the servant collapses — the man’s own exhaustion and longing shown through them.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 借酒浇愁，想让思念暂时停下来，却说明思念有多深。
imagery.en: He drinks to keep the longing at bay — which only shows how deep it runs.
